events.system:
P = 1-(4-ethynylphenyl)ethan-1-one
P --[dil. H₂SO₄, HgSO₄, 333 K]--> Q
Q --[Ph₃P=CH₂]--> R
R --[OsO₄, NMO]--> S
S --[KMnO₄, H⁺, heat]--> T
Q --[NH₂OH·HCl, pyridine]--> U
events.hidden_link: P has an alkyne and a ketone. Hydration of the alkyne gives a ketone (Markovnikov), not an aldehyde. So Q is a diketone. Wittig on Q gives a diene R. OsO4 on R gives a tetraol S (syn dihydroxylation). KMnO4/H+ oxidises the primary alcohols of S to carboxylic acids T. Q with NH2OH gives a dioxime U.
events.route: 1. Identify P. 2. React P with HgSO4/H2SO4: terminal alkyne hydrates to methyl ketone -> Q. 3. React Q with Ph3P=CH2: both ketones become alkenes -> R. 4. React R with OsO4: both alkenes become diols -> S. 5. React S with KMnO4/H+: primary alcohols become carboxylic acids, tertiary alcohols are untouched -> T. 6. React Q with NH2OH: both ketones become oximes -> U.
events.student_must_notice: The regioselectivity of the alkyne hydration (gives methyl ketone, not aldehyde) and the selectivity of KMnO4 oxidation on S (primary alcohols to acids, tertiary unaffected, not aldehydes).
events.trap: Hydrating the alkyne to an aldehyde (anti-Markovnikov) or under-oxidising the primary alcohols in S to aldehydes (using KMnO4).

P: 1-(4-ethynylphenyl)ethan-1-one (acetyl attached to phenyl bearing terminal alkyne at para). Dil H2SO4/HgSO4/333K hydrates terminal alkyne to give methyl ketone (Markovnikov addition), producing Q = 1-(4-(1-hydroxyethyl)phenyl)ethan-1-one (i.e., phenyl-CH(OH)-CH3 at para). Q does not contain an aldehyde, so Tollens' test negative → (A) correct.
Ph3P=CH2 (Wittig) converts the ketone of Q to an alkene R (phenyl-CH=CH-CH3 at para).
OsO4/NMO dihydroxylates the alkene to give vicinal cis-diol S.
KMnO4/H+, heat cleaves the diol (or the alkene if not fully oxidized) to give a diacid T (or carboxylic acids). Acidic T reacts with NaHCO3 to release CO2 → effervescence → (B) correct.
2,4-DNP test detects aldehydes/ketones; T is a diacid, no carbonyl → (C) false.
U is formed from Q with NH2OH·HCl/pyridine, likely oxidizes the primary alcohol (if present) to a carbonyl; stereochemistry: Q's alcohol is secondary? Actually Q after hydration gives secondary alcohol (CH(OH)CH3). Oxidation of secondary alcohol does not give stereoisomer; only possible if there was a chiral center? The para position on phenyl does not create new stereocenter; thus number of stereoisomers for U is 1, not 3 → (D) false.
Thus correct options: A and B.

members.working: P (p-ethynyl acetophenone) undergoes Hg²⁺-catalyzed hydration of the terminal alkyne (Markovnikov) to give Q = 1,4-diacetylbenzene (p-C6H4(COCH3)2). (A) Q is a ketone only, no aldehyde → negative Tollens' test: correct. Q + Ph3P=CH2 methylenates both ketones → R = p-divinylbenzene. OsO4/NMO syn-dihydroxylates both vinyl groups → S = p-bis(1,2-dihydroxyethyl)benzene. Hot acidic KMnO4 cleaves each glycol (each side chain loses both carbons) → T = terephthalic acid, p-C6H4(COOH)2. (B) T is a dicarboxylic acid → effervescence (CO2) with NaHCO3: correct. (C) T has no carbonyl (C=O) group → negative 2,4-DNP test: incorrect. Q + NH2OH·HCl gives U = bis-oxime of 1,4-diacetylbenzene. Each C=N oxime shows E/Z isomerism; by molecular symmetry (para-disubstituted, identical groups) the EE and ZZ forms are distinct while EZ = ZE, giving 3 stereoisomers: (D) correct.
